text_blocks.snippet: Early symptoms of type 2 diabetes develop slowly over time, and many people have no symptoms at all in the early stages.

list.snippet: Frequent urination: Your kidneys work harder to get rid of extra sugar in your blood, making you use the bathroom more often, especially at night.
Increased thirst: Because you are peeing more, your body loses extra fluid, which leads to ongoing thirst.
Constant fatigue: Your cells cannot absorb sugar properly for energy, leaving you feeling tired and weak even after sleeping.
Increased hunger: Your body misses out on energy from glucose, which can make you feel hungry soon after eating.
Blurred vision: High blood sugar changes the fluid levels and shape of the lens in your eye.
Slow-healing cuts and sores: High sugar levels impair circulation and your immune system, making minor wounds heal slowly.
Frequent infections: Yeast infections, skin infections, or urinary tract infections happen more easily when extra sugar feeds bacteria and yeast.
Tingling or numbness: Mild nerve irritation or tingling in the hands or feet can start early on.
Darkened skin patches: Velvety, dark skin (called acanthosis nigricans) on the neck, armpits, or groin can signal insulin resistance.

text_blocks.snippet: You can read more about risk factors and warning signs on the Mayo Clinic or the WebMD guide to diabetes symptoms.

perspectives.title: 🚨 5 warning signs your body may be developing insulin resistance or prediabetes. Don’t ignore them. Diabetes doesn’t always appear overnight. Your body often gives subtle warning signs months or even years before blood sugar levels become severely abnormal. ⚠️ Watch out for these common symptoms: ✔️ Constant fatigue despite adequate sleep ✔️ Tingling or numbness in your hands and feet ✔️ Excessive hunger and excessive thirst ✔️ Frequent urination, especially at night ✔️ Dark, velvety patches around the neck, underarms, knees, or knuckles (Acanthosis Nigricans) These symptoms can be associated with insulin resistance a condition that often develops before type 2 diabetes. While these signs don’t confirm diabetes on their own, they are important reasons to get evaluated. Early diagnosis and lifestyle changes can significantly reduce the risk of developing type 2 diabetes. 💬 Have you noticed any of these symptoms?
